racecards.race_name: Bet 30 Get 5 Weekly betstgeorge.com Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Talented mare and very difficult to oppose given what she's up against here
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner who was competitive in bumpers there; won a maiden hurdle before finishing close up under a big weight on handicap debut at Aintree (2m4f, good to soft), and a combination of 3m on tiring ground is good reason to turn a blind eye to her no-show in a Listed race for mares at Doncaster; difficult to oppose given what she's up against here.

stable_tour.quote: She had some nice form in Ireland and is a big, strong, scopey sort who finished third in a maiden hurdle at Fontwell on her first start for us. It was a good run and she took a good blow jumping the second-last, so I think there should be plenty of improvement to come and I'd hope she'd go well next time in a 2m4f mares' maiden hurdle. She should make a chaser in time. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Irish point winner; disappointing in a bumper but surely he's better than that
runners.spotlight: Bought for 62,000GBP after winning an Irish point on yielding to soft in November; offered little in a Southwell bumper (soft; 10-1) but highly likely that he's capable of better than that.

runners.comment: No show in bumpers; 100-1 when pulled up on her hurdling introduction at Plumpton
runners.spotlight: No show in a couple of bumpers and was 100-1 when pulled up on her hurdling introduction at Plumpton.

racecards.verdict: Dan Skelton's BROOMFIELD ADERRA was progressing nicely until last time and on all known form this looks her's to lose.

runners.owner: A Lewers D Shaw A Irvine
runners.comment: Three-time winner but arrives here in no sort of form and all headgear now left off
runners.spotlight: Three-time winner but arrives here in no sort of form and the new blinkers (replacing usual cheekpieces) did nothing for him two weeks ago; now goes in no headgear; risky.

runners.owner: S Packham, A Austin And B Austin
runners.comment: Has back-class but he's been struggling for a while now under both codes
runners.spotlight: Listed Flat winner for Aidan O'Brien; made a successful hurdle debut for this yard in early 2024 but it's been a struggle since then under both codes and he's tough to trust at the minute.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qual') (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I expected Peking Opera to run very well but I've had two good horses run in this race in the last two years and they were beaten. He's always been a bit lazy at home but is a different horse in the track. You could work him with a donkey and he'd be quite happy to work with it. I thought given his Flat form he'd want a stiff two miles but he's shown he's got a bit of pace. He'll probably run in the Adonis at Kempton next - Gary Moore, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Yeats Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Peking Opera has done well over the winter and is a horse that is going to stay very well. He could be one for something like the Queen's Vase over 1m6f at Ascot. You could bring him back a fraction to 1m4f. He has good options and he did well to win on seasonal debut - Chris Armstrong, stable's representative.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Peking Opera had a lovely run on his debut at Naas, and his work has stepped up since. Seamus gave him a lovely ride. It's nice to get a win with him as a two-year-old and he'll be a horse to look forward to next year over a trip. That might be him done for the year, we'll see how he comes out of it - Chris Armstrong, representing Aidan O'Brien.

stable_tour.quote: He won a Listed race at Navan last time and stays well. He came out of that in good order and the Queen's Vase is definitely a possibility for him. 15-06-23

He looked good on his first start over hurdles at Sandown but he was getting a lot of weight from his rivals and then he fell at the last when beaten in the Adonis. He's been disappointing in four runs on the Flat but should be suited by stepping up in trip in handicap hurdles. 29-10-24

runners.comment: Last two runs (hurdle/AW) weren't his best but his form here heightens interest
runners.spotlight: Four Flat wins and three over hurdles; has yet to win this season over jumps but two of his three placed efforts came here and he's likely to be a strong contender, for all that last two runs (hurdle/AW) weren't his best.

quotes.race: Jordan Road Surfacing Highways Solution Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Motazzen has his mojo working at the moment, and to be honest he's been well placed, too. The race cut up, but it's still brilliant how he picked up. He was having a good old look around in front - Paul O'Brien, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: We acquired this son of Dubawi from the Shadwell dispersal, having won twice in France for Jean-Claude Rouget over 1m2½f and 1m5f. We have had him gelded and he appears to be showing more speed than he did in France. His work has been pleasing and there are a couple of handicaps next week at Chester I have in mind. He came highly recommended from Shadwell, and it made sense for us to buy him. He is a very interesting newcomer to the team. 27-04-22

runners.comment: Lightly raced and this marked step up in trip could benefit on her handicap debut
runners.spotlight: No match for an easy odds-on winner in her latest maiden and those behind weren't a great bunch; however, she's lightly raced and this marked step up in trip could benefit on her handicap debut.

runners.comment: Ability respected but there are wellbeing issues after so long out
runners.spotlight: Very nearly won over C&D last January and that was only three starts ago; feasible excuses since then as probably failed to stay 3m1f and then bled here when last seen a year ago; ability respected but there are wellbeing issues after so long out.

runners.comment: Back from another layoff but a winner last time and still lightly raced; raised 6lb
runners.spotlight: Second run back from an absence of 679 days when the decisive winner of a 2m3f handicap here in May of last year (good ground); now back from another layoff but probably has it in her to cope with the 6lb higher mark.

runners.comment: He was looking when regressive but did run better to finish a 14l third at Taunton
runners.spotlight: He was looking when regressive even before pulling up in his first two runs for this yard but ran better at Taunton (2m3f, good; ridden by Kayla Ruddy), where he was no match for the front two but did come from well off the pace; possibilities; 1lb wrong.

racecards.verdict: The suggestion is MOTAZZEN (nap) who has a good record at this track. Geordies Betty is the second choice.

runners.comment: Consistent gelding with C&D form and needs respecting
runners.spotlight: Both wins have come in the mud at Leicester where he ran another respectable race three weeks ago (good to soft); has C&D form and needs respecting.

runners.comment: Chase winner in Ireland; two good runs since wind op; long absence to overcome

runners.owner: Miss Jane Edgar & D V Gardner

runners.breeder: Mrs Catherine Bodin & Mr Joel Bodin

runners.comment: Showed a bit in bumpers, though was no closer than 16l in any of them
runners.spotlight: Showed a bit in bumpers, though was no closer than 16l in any of them; best watched on this hurdling introduction.

stable_tour.quote: A bonny little horse who has been second, fourth and third in three bumpers. He was a real cheapie, he was literally the last one through the sales ring at Doncaster and Ruth, my wife, said, “I'm having him!” He's a fun horse and I've been delighted with those runs in bumpers. He's going to go hurdling now and will be fun round the gaff tracks for his new owners. He's just tweaked a muscle in his backside and will be off for a couple of weeks, but when we get that right he'll be out hurdling. I think it'll be handicaps for him further down the line - I wouldn't have thought he'd be winning a novice. 03-12-25

runners.comment: Bumper efforts make for better reading than his two tailed-off efforts over hurdles
runners.spotlight: Bumper efforts make for better reading than his two tailed-off efforts over hurdles; one for another day.

runners.comment: Held every chance when falling in third Irish point; has shown some promise under rules
runners.spotlight: Held every chance when falling in his third Irish point; has shown some promise under rules (bumper/maiden) without suggesting he'll be troubling Unknown Entity.

runners.comment: Beaten 33l and 51l in two runs over hurdles, though the latest was behind Sober Glory
runners.spotlight: Second in an Irish point; beaten 33l and 51l in two runs over hurdles, though the latest was behind Sober Glory at Newbury; this isn't anything like so demanding as that race was.

runners.comment: Never threatening and tailed off in a soft-ground Chepstow bumper two months ago (16-1)
runners.spotlight: Never threatening and tailed off in a soft-ground Chepstow bumper two months ago (16-1).

runners.comment: 5-25 on the Flat; 33-1 and tailed off on hurdle debut when in a different yard
runners.spotlight: Had plenty of Flat racing on the continent, going 5-25; 33-1 and tailed off in a good-ground maiden hurdle at Taunton in January and has since left Tom George.

runners.comment: Major form claims and hard to beat if accepting the two new forms of headgear
runners.spotlight: Ex-Willie Mullins; eye-catching third on stable debut at Ludlow (2m, good to soft), then went close at Wincanton and wasn't disgraced in the always-strong EBF Final at Sandown (2m4f, soft) 20 days ago; provided he accepts the two new forms of headgear he should be hard to beat.

runners.owner: Galloping On The South Downs Partnership
runners.comment: Advanced his RPR despite finishing last of the nine runners in a bumper at Ascot
runners.spotlight: Advanced his RPR despite finishing last of the nine runners in a bumper at Ascot where he was only 7l off the winner; should have a future over hurdles.

runners.owner: D S Dennis & John Hw Finch
runners.comment: A disappointing favourite when beaten 20l in a juvenile hurdle here in November
runners.spotlight: A disappointing favourite when beaten 20l in a juvenile hurdle here in November (good to soft); market strength would imply that he's no doubt capable of better.

racecards.race_name: betstgeorge.com With Daily St George Specials Chase Series Final (A Handicap Chase) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Consistent in victory and defeat this season; has run well on his two previous visits here
runners.spotlight: Back from a break with three excellent efforts and he's only 3lb higher than when winning at Doncaster the last time (November; 2m3f, good to soft); has run well on his two previous visits here.

stable_tour.quote: He started the season off in style with an easy win at Plumpton in a 2m novice hurdle and was a one-length second to Attacca under a penalty at Kempton. I thought he would run well going back to Kempton at Christmas but he found the soft ground too much and could not pick up his feet in it. The experience will have taught him plenty and he will have plenty of decent opportunities in the spring when the ground dries a little. The handicapper dropped him 2lb to 123 and I think this progressive youngster is above standard and, like so many of his family, he will be better on better ground. 11-01-23

prev_owners.owner: Mme Isabelle Gallorini, Haras De Saint-Voir & J-M Baudrelle

runners.comment: A 13l winner on soft here last time and a 6lb rise could have been worse
runners.spotlight: Back on song when a 13l winner from Rip Wheeler over C&D two weeks ago, seeing it out stronger than the second on the soft ground; the returning cheekpieces did him no harm and a clear contender despite going up 6lb; all three wins have been on soft or heavy.

stable_tour.quote: He's an interesting recruit from France, lightly raced and open to improvement. A hurdles winner at Auteuil, he finished runner-up in a couple of chases and looks to be on an attractive mark. I've been in no rush with him as he wants soft ground. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Tired behind Mon Champion last time but this drier surface brings him into it
runners.spotlight: Has won three of his six starts over fences and perhaps found the ground too soft when a tired second behind Mon Champion over C&D recently, as he looked threatening until late on; this surface brings him into it.

stable_tour.quote: A nice big horse who was immature last season. His best run came on his last start at Huntingdon, but he was too gangly to do himself justice. He's a well-handicapped horse who will improve for a fence this season. 28-10-25

runners.comment: Dual chase winner who has been running better than his recent heavy defeats may imply
runners.spotlight: Dual chase winner who has been running better than his recent heavy defeats may imply and he's on a good mark with Harry Cobden booked; off since October.

stable_tour.quote: He's tough and genuine and, although he beat absolutely nothing in winning a maiden hurdle at Taunton and a novice at Hereford, I loved the way he went about it. He could give us some sport on spring ground, although he doesn't want it too deep. I'd say his next race will be a handicap off 112 and he'll be smashing over a fence next season. 28-02-24

runners.comment: C&D winner; when a 6l third off this mark at Sedgefield his jumping could have been better
runners.spotlight: Won over hurdles prior to his successful chase debut over C&D (soft) and when a 6l third off this mark at Sedgefield his jumping could have been better; needs considering.

quotes.race: Ayrshire Cancer Support Masquerade Ball Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Alright Dai went up 12lb in the handicap for his Market Rasen win and we had him entered up in case the handicapper did something like that. He was placed in bumpers and a novice hurdle so does have form and maybe dropping him out has suited him the last twice - Neil Mulholland, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He took to fences very well, winning on his chasing debut at Fontwell. That was on soft ground, which wouldn't have been ideal, as he'd prefer nice ground, but it was a winnable opportunity so we let him take his chance. He's had 15 runs, winning four times and finishing second twice, and in seven of those runs he's been in the first three, so he's a good solid horse at a level. He jumps well. 04-02-26

runners.comment: Stuck to his task and just got the better of Le Galli Bier for 2nd last time at Plumpton
runners.spotlight: Can be a bit in and out but he stuck to his task and just got the better of Le Galli Bier for second last time at Plumpton (2m4f, soft); however, the winner left both behind and this 9yo is off the same mark.

quotes.race: Daily Offers With BetMGM Handicap Chase (Fontwell Chase Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Koenigsstern had been running really well without winning, but here I thought he jumped incredibly well. He'd already qualified for the final before this, but we want to keep them running and this looked like the right race, but the final will be the target now. All of my horses are running really well, so long may it continue - Nick Gifford, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won a handicap chase at Fontwell on Boxing Day last year. He was in at Plumpton on Monday, but we decided to wait and may now go to Fontwell next week, which is probably the sensible option. He's the sort who'll win a race every season. 03-12-25

runners.comment: Consistent but he has been edging up the weights and he's 2lb out of the handicap here
runners.spotlight: Made a winning debut for Chris Gordon in September and has continued to run well in defeat; this longer trip shouldn't be a problem but he has been edging up the weights and he's 2lb out of the handicap here.

stable_tour.quote: I think he's very good fun in 0-100 2m chases. He got a little win at Worcester in September and he ran very well again to come third at Warwick the other day. He's running very consistently but he doesn't find much off the bridle, so we might ride him a little bit cold and try to deliver him on the line. He's a tough horse who seems to take his races well and hopefully his time will come again this season. 01-12-25

runners.breeder: Ecurie Domaine De Baune, Francois Thomas
runners.comment: Hasn't been finding masses in the finishes of his races and he's 2lb wrong
runners.spotlight: Twelve defeats divided equally between hurdles and fences; hasn't been finding masses in the finishes of his races and he's 2lb wrong.

stable_tour.quote: Placed in both starts for us last season, his rating is modest but he's a half-brother to Le Patron and will win races. He was too fresh when disappointing at Fontwell on Sunday, but he's already run over fences in France, so has the option of going four-year-old novice chasing. He schools well and it might make sense to go over a fence now. 28-10-25

racecards.verdict: Back on a less taxing surface, RIP WHEELER has a sporting chance of reversing recent course placings with Mon Champion.

runners.owner: Harry Fry Racing Syndicate Hello Cello

runners.spotlight: Won a 2m3f handicap hurdle here in October under Ciaran O'Shea (good to soft) and chasing hasn't gone to plan since then; respected back in this discipline as she's not handicapped out of it.

runners.comment: Has been struggling under both codes and new cheekpieces need to make a difference
runners.spotlight: Has finished runner-up on the Flat and over hurdles but has been struggling under both codes since returning from more than three months off; the new cheekpieces will need to make a difference.

stable_tour.quote: He was bought as a dual-purpose horse and ran a nice race when second last time at Plumpton. He could pinch a little maiden and we'll see what there is around Easter. He'll qualify for a mark after his next run. He's no world-beater but I think he's going to be a good, fun horse over hurdles and on the Flat. 26-02-25

runners.breeder: Razza Del Sole Societa Agricola Srl
runners.comment: A chance on some of his form but he's looking a hard horse to predict
runners.spotlight: Sole success in 18 starts came in a maiden here in 2023; went close back here on December's return from a mammoth absence and his fourth to Tommy Dillon two runs ago wasn't too bad a run; does seem hard to predict, however.

runners.comment: Has no clear form claims and she was 50-1 for handicap debut last time and ran accordingly
runners.spotlight: Has no obvious form claims; 50-1 for handicap debut last time and ran accordingly.

runners.comment: Uncompetitive in his first three races; the market can guide on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Uncompetitive in his first three races, although it was a competitive novice he contested at Newbury (2m, beaten 45l; 200-1) in January; pulled up at Lingfield (2m4f, heavy) latest; the market can guide on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Poor latest run but was second then first in two races on his return to hurdling
runners.spotlight: Tailed off last time but had appreciated the return to hurdles with a second here (beaten 16l) before a 3l success at Lingfield (2m, heavy); he's able on good to soft ground if he can shrug aside that poor last run.

quotes.race: At The Races App Expert Tips Conditional Jockeys' Training Series Handicap Hurdle (Part Of The REI)
quotes.quote: It was Tommy Dillion's first run for a long time but it was the ideal race for him and the conditions were perfect. If he hadn't had as many problems as he's had, he'd probably have been rated in the 120s, but he has been fragile and has the best owners in the world - Richard Rowe, trainer.

racecards.verdict: The one with the most obvious upside is handicap newcomer TEST THE MARKET who ran up against a fair sort last time.

runners.spotlight: Didn't run badly when fourth of eight at Chelmsford a fortnight ago (blinkered first time; ridden by Jack Loughnane); dropped another 3lb since; each-way shout.

quotes.race: Win £1M With BetMGM's Golden Goals Handicap
quotes.quote: Tadreeb is obviously in very good form and we've been very lucky to inherit him, as he's a very nice horse. He's got very good back form and was quite classy in his day. Michael [Attwater, previous trainer] did very well with him, but sometimes a change of yard can just perk them up again. We'll be looking at running him here next week - Rod Millman, trainer.

quotes.race: MansionBet Proud Partners Of The AWC Handicap
quotes.quote: Tadreeb has to be ridden like that and it was a muddling pace. I think the plan is to run him on Good Friday if the handicapper allows. He could be a nice type for the turf - William Carson, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He was a nice horse for Mark Johnston. I train for Canisbay, who have a lot of horses based at Epsom but some with me as well. Michael Attwater had a really good time with Tadreeb but then he lost his form a little bit and the owner decided he wanted to see if a change of scenery would do him good. We haven't got the gallops and facilities of Epsom - we're a small family-run business and have our own gallops - but sometimes these horses appreciate a bit of an easier regime. We gave him a nice rest through last summer and he won his first few races when we brought him back in January. Unfortunately, he pulled a muscle, which is why he's missed a bit of the season, but he's come back in good form. He's seven now, so he isn't going to get any better, but he's won three and been placed several times this year. He should give us fun through the winter. 27-08-25

runners.comment: Won twice on AW last September; quiet this year and may need an ease in grade

runners.comment: Had a fine winter but she seems to have peaked and this is a rise in class

runners.spotlight: Creditable third on his stable debut at Wolverhampton in January (6f; hooded first time, absent today); still to prove his stamina for 7f; tongue tied today; withdrawn after breaking out of the stalls at Kempton this month.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (Plus 10 Race)

stable_tour.quote: He's new to the yard. We've given his wind a little tweak. He has shown some decent form in the past and looks quite well treated. He might be ok on soft ground and if I didn't have to tweak his wind he'd have been out earlier. 17-04-24

runners.comment: Three course wins this winter; not at best last time but he looks the type to bounce back
runners.spotlight: Disappointed over 7f here four weeks ago but this trip probably suits better and he isn't handicapped out of things judged on his previous second here; wouldn't be ideally suited by a tactical event.

quotes.race: BetUK. Home Of The Acca Handicap
quotes.quote: The Craftymaster has been a revelation. He used to be slow, but stayed. Now, when that was going to turn into a sprint, I was thinking you can't go wide as you'll never win, so just wait and see if you outstay them. He's put them to bed in half a furlong with his injection of speed. He's learning and getting better at everything he does. This was the first test of his mettle, a full field with horses who have been in very good form and he's up to it. I don't feel I'm at the bottom of him yet - I feel if something came at him he'd go again -  William Carson, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: BetUK. It's Where The UK Bets Handicap
quotes.quote: The Craftymaster has developed late and we've been very lucky to have him. He's progressing really nicely. He's going up the grades slowly and he's coping with it. He stays very well and he's lazy through his races, so you'd like to think there's always just a tiny little bit left. We'll keep going forward - Tony Carroll, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: All three wins have come here and he ran pretty well on his sole previous attempt at 2m

runners.comment: Promise two starts ago but down the field last time and could do with settling better

runners.comment: Three wins from last four starts; there can be optimism he has more left in the tank

runners.spotlight: Ran well in fourth at Chelmsford (2m, Polytrack) in January when back from some time off and built on that to go close there (1m6f) four weeks ago; there's every chance he'll be bang there once more.

runners.comment: Hard to fancy on the face of it but lightly raced & the longer trip is an interesting move

quotes.race: Make The Move To Midnite Handicap

quotes.race: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: We got Sea Legend but he had a problem in behind so he had to have a long time off. We gelded him and the last month he's gone nicely. He enjoyed that trip, he's got a big, long stride and I'm really pleased with that on his first run back. It was a relief to go to the races and run so well. I think he'll be suited by a mile and a half and we'll look at all the options in those nice handicaps. That was his first run for a year, so we wanted to get it out the way before making plans - James Fanshawe, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice, big horse. He's had problems but I'm hopefully quite good at fixing them. I'm looking forward to him, mainly for his pedigree. Sea The Stars was one of my favourite horses and he's good at producing top horses. 07-05-25

quotes.race: Sky Bet Extra Places Every Day Handicap

This looked a competitive event but he won well enough. At some point we'll try him over a mile again but there's no rush - Grant Tuer, trainer.

quotes.race: Due Diligence Standing At Whitsbury Manor British EBF Blagrave Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was very straightforward, very professional and Bahan Bandit travelled nicely. We thought we would sit back before getting a tone of the race but when the split came he got his head down and found the gap nicely. We tried him on the grass last year and he didn't really look like he suited it but my horses are running much better this year and that is sometimes how it goes. We were thinking about the Gosforth Park Cup as he's unbeaten over five furlongs at Newcastle, and there's also a big five-furlong handicap at Ascot in July - we had that in mind thinking that a stiff five at Ascot would suit him - Ruth Carr, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a classy horse who is new to us having been acquired out of Ruth Carr's yard following four wins this year. He joins the yard with a rating of 100 and I must praise Ruth, who did a great job with him - I've been very pleased with him since he arrived. We're going to stick to what we know he does best and that is sprint handicaps. He ran in a 5f handicap at Newcastle last week, coming from off the pace to finish a highly creditable second. Looking ahead, there is the Portland Handicap and the 6f International Handicap at York we may consider. 06-09-23

runners.comment: Useful for Karl Burke but didn't progress last year; best watched on return for new yard
runners.spotlight: Looked promising at two but didn't really kick on last year, with fifth his best placing in four handicap starts to end the season; sold out of Karl Burke's stable for 27,000gns last autumn; a watching brief is the percentage call on reappearance.

stable_tour.quote: He's a high-class horse. He'll have an entry in the Norfolk Stakes as well ? Steve Parkin [owner whose horses run under the Clipper Logistics banner] was keen to put him in, in case it's a weak race ? but for me the Coventry should be the race. His half-sister Dramatised won the Queen Mary there and the track should hold no fears for him. He looks very exciting. 10-06-24

runners.comment: Promising fourth on C&D reappearance but only sixth of seven at Lingfield since
runners.spotlight: Promising reappearance after wind surgery when fourth of 14 over C&D in January but failed to build on that when only sixth of seven at Lingfield (6f) four weeks ago; bounce back needed.

stable_tour.quote: I thought the race at Newcastle last month would just take the freshness out of him, but he won very nicely and we're very hopeful he'll keep progressing at 6f this season. His owners like to be represented at the big festivals and I think he's the right kind of horse for that. 04-04-24

runners.comment: Did well over 6f on turf last year, including two wins; first start for 139 days
runners.spotlight: Winner of 6f handicaps at York (good to firm) and Ayr (soft) last year; finished off with a good third in a big field at Doncaster in November; no great record when fresh.

quotes.race: Churchill Tyres Handicap
quotes.quote: Jimmy [Sullivan] gave Rousing Encore a lovely ride. We thought we were maybe drawn on the wrong side, he likes some cover but we didn't want to be too far back because it's hard to make up ground on a fast track on fast ground. Jimmy edged over onto the rail and the horse put his head down and battled well for him. There are plenty of decent six-furlong races for us to go at - Ruth Carr, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a consistent sort who came here from Richard Fahey's last summer. With a rating of 84, he'll be chasing some valuable pots and is entered for a Newbury handicap on Friday, which will be his first race of the year. Newbury is a long way to go for us, so I hope the journey is worthwhile. 09-04-25

runners.comment: Below par both runs this year but this former course scorer is back on a workable mark
runners.spotlight: Below par in two AW outings this year but might have been building up his fitness and this former course scorer is starting to look well treated on the pick of last year's turf form; no shock were he to bounce back to form.

quotes.race: JKR Industrial Cleaning Ltd Handicap
quotes.quote: Venture Capital showed a lot of speed last time at Thirsk and immediately after the race my old man felt that sprinting could be his gig and he's shown that there. It was only his first try over six furlongs so I'd like to think there's a lot more to come from him. There's some nice sprints in the summer and he's shown he handles the ground there. We'll see what the handicapper does but he could progress now at that trip. The time was good there and in these big sprint handicaps you need a horse that stays the trip well so that's a big positive. We'll see what comes up but I'm sure by the end of the year there will be bigger and better things on the horizon - Adam Ryan, trainer's son and assistant.

stable_tour.quote: He's very genuine and we've been very lucky with the sire's progeny. He's a homebred and the owner's first winner and I can see them having some good fun with him on turf. He'll get a mile no problem and we'll look for a nice handicap and work from there. 04-04-24

runners.breeder: J P M Main &  Andrew Knott
runners.comment: All eight wins on turf but placed here last summer and has a reasonable record fresh
runners.spotlight: This 8yo has gained all eight career wins on turf but does have placed form on AW (including over 7f here last summer); also has a reasonable record when fresh so no surprise to see him go well for a yard that is no stranger to Newcastle success.

quotes.race: Ascot Shop Handicap
quotes.quote: Mister Bluebird's dam won this race seven years ago and he is her only foal, so it's a good story. We wanted to see if he'd get this trip and Rossa [Ryan, jockey] felt this stiff six was just what he wanted. He was having a good look at the stand too. We'll wait for the handicapper and then see what we do next - Heather Main, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap
quotes.quote: Mister Bluebird was very straightforward last year and unlucky not to win. He got the job done today and I'm pleased for the horse. - William Buick, rider

runners.comment: Good AW record includes comfortable C&D win last month; creditable third since; player
runners.spotlight: His good 5-15 AW record includes a comfortable C&D win from the front last month; creditable third of nine at Chelmsford (5f) since and the form of that race has been boosted; a must for the shortlist.

runners.comment: No win since spring 2022; struggled in Dubai this year; belated AW debut
runners.spotlight: Losing run goes back nearly four years; no impact in sprint handicaps on turf at Meydan this year and makes a very belated AW debut on his return to Britain.

quotes.race: Cazoo Temple Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Twilight Calls is getting better. He loves really rattling fast ground, but you can't blame the ground today. He wasn't totally lucky in-running but take nothing away from the winner. Adam [Kirby] said the faster they go the better and I think if Wesley Ward appears at Ascot, that shouldn't be a problem. They go a million miles an hour [in the King's Stand] and hopefully it will be firm ground as well - Henry Candy, trainer.

quotes.race: Price Promise At bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: Twilight Falls has matured since last year and must have fast ground and five furlongs. The plan is to bring him back for the Group 3 Palace Stakes on Guineas weekend - Henry Candy, trainer.

quotes.race: Moet & Chandon Handicap
quotes.quote: Twilight Calls was doing too much in a small field over 6f at Leicester last time and was suited by this drop back in trip - David Probert, jockey.

runners.comment: Back from break with a fair run last month; won competitive race off this mark last year
runners.spotlight: Back from three months off to finish a respectable fifth of 12 at Southwell five weeks ago; has returned to the same mark as when winning a competitive Racing League Handicap on turf last summer; dangerous to dismiss.

stable_tour.quote: I think he can win a race or two before the end of the year as he's going the right way. He handles ease in the ground and stays well over a fast-run 6f, while a sharp 7f wouldn't bother him either. He's a bit of a stresshead who's hard on himself at home, but when he's on a going day he can be competitive. He looked unlucky at York two starts ago when he flew home on ground he didn't like. He's ready to start winning again and Ayr's big meeting could be in the pipeline for him. 07-08-25

runners.comment: Remains 4lb higher than Windsor win last year and career best needed on return (gelded)
runners.spotlight: AW novice winner who landed a 6f Windsor handicap off 4lb lower last summer; failed to reproduce that form in three subsequent outings last year but there were excuses on two of those occasions; will need a career best on reappearance (has been gelded).

stable_tour.quote: He ran well at Kempton on his reappearance, just getting tired late on. He'll be a useful sprint handicapper this year, with all roads hopefully leading to Ascot. 22-04-25

runners.comment: Easy wins in two 0-65s last autumn; this is a lot harder but could be plenty more to come
runners.spotlight: Much improved sent handicapping after wind surgery, easily winning 0-65s over 6f at Lingfield (AW) and Thirsk (soft) last September; this represents a significant hike in grade but there's almost certainly more to come from this very lightly raced 4yo.

racecards.verdict: Power Fizz (second choice) and Hockney look capable of better but TWILIGHT FUN could have a fitness edge over them.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Power Fizz, 5/1 Twilight Fun, 8/1 Paddy's Day,  Badri, 10/1 Wicket Keeper,  Wheels Of Fire,  Hockney, 11/1 Sergeant Wilko, 12/1 Rousing Encore,  Venture Capital, 16/1 Mister Bluebird, 20/1 Roberto Caro, 25/1 Andesite,  Twilight Calls

racecards.race_name: Friday Night Live With SBK Handicap

runners.comment: Well held at Southwell latest but good C&D record (three wins) provides hope for a revival
runners.spotlight: All three wins over C&D, the latest in September; failed to build on his quite promising reappearance when well beaten at Southwell five weeks ago but capable of staging a revival back at Newcastle.

quotes.race: Mini Golf At High Gosforth Park Handicap
quotes.quote: That was pretty straightforward. I was a little bit worried about the draw but I had a plan in my head how to ride Rogue Encore and the race itself fell better for me. Peter [Chapple-Hyam, trainer] gave me plenty of confidence when I said I knew what I wanted to do and I relaxed beautifully early, got a nice clean run and stayed the trip really well. He's a horse who loves it up here - P J McDonald, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: This colt has a nice pedigree and he looks to have ability to match. His training is going very well and the plan will be to start him off in the next month. His work has been good and he will be another for the 'Rogues' to look forward to. 06-07-23

runners.comment: Some good form last summer and recent reappearance third quite encouraging; considered
runners.spotlight: His progress stalled in the autumn but he resumed with quite an encouraging third over the extended 1m at Wolverhampton a fortnight ago; nicely treated on the form he showed in some turf handicaps at the end of last summer; needs considering.

runners.comment: 2-2 at Southwell (7f/1m) since joining this yard; impressed latest and bold bid likely
runners.spotlight: Has taken his AW record to 4-7 when winning twice at Southwell (7f/1m) since joining James Horton; raised 6lb since last time but the way he moved into contention suggests there's likely even more to come for his new stable.

quotes.race: DragonBet Some Might Lay Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Kieran [Shoemark, jockey], very kindly, slightly held up his hands and felt he had gone a fraction too soon on Saytarr. He had to use up a lot of petrol at Southwell last time and he's had a hard race today. There's definitely wins to be had with him - Charlie Fellowes, trainer.

runners.comment: Progressive on turf; hasn't translated that to AW on last two starts but still early days
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo who has progressive turf form; hasn't translated that to AW in two attempts but still early days and it's possible he needed last month's reappearance after wind surgery.

runners.comment: Good fourth over C&D last summer and won on turf for new yard in autumn; respected
runners.spotlight: Ended his time with Henry de Bromhead with a good fourth in a Racing League handicap over C&D and struck at the second time of asking for Roger Fell in 7f Newmarket handicap in October; only nudged up 2lb and can go well if ready to roll after five months off.

runners.comment: Four-time course scorer who has placed on AW in Ireland on last three starts; claims
runners.spotlight: Four-time course scorer (6f/7f) for William Haggas; struggled on turf in Ireland for this yard last autumn but has found form again since returning to AW, placing three times at Dundalk (7f/1m) in recent months; has to enter calculations for a stable with a good record in Britain.

quotes.race: Try Unibet's New Acca Boosts Handicap
quotes.quote: It looked as though there'd be a good bit of pace on and it worked out that way. Going back up to 7f at a track he's won at before probably all helped but I think Brewing is a horse who is really learning how to drop into gear now, he's been winning but has still looking a bit immature about it but tonight he was direct and true. It was a good performance - Tom Marquand, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: C&D winner last autumn; better than result when sixth over 7f here on final start
runners.spotlight: Reacted well to blinkers at the end of 2025, including a C&D win in October; slowly away and caught the eye with his late headway into sixth over 7f here on his final start in December; returns from 112 days off with the blinkers replaced by second-time cheekpieces.

stable_tour.quote: He's £1,500 very well spent as he's earned nearly £32,000 for us. He's a funny horse with loads of talent and, although he's only won once, he's kept bringing in good prize-money, so I accept it. You have to humour him and do things on his terms - I think he nearly shocked himself when he won at Newcastle this month. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Didn't win often but was regularly placed in Ireland for Andy Slattery; first run for yard
runners.spotlight: Won only two of his 32 starts in Ireland for Andy Slattery but he did finish in the first three in half of them, including third in a 1m Dundalk claimer six weeks ago; first run for new yard.

prev_owners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

runners.comment: Placed three times (for new yard latest) and brings unexposed potential to handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Placed twice in turf maidens in Ireland for Aidan O'Brien last October; tongue-tied first time, similar form when 6l third in C&D novice for new yard last month; hard to argue his opening mark looks generous but he brings unexposed potential.

runners.comment: C&D win in January; went close to another last time; up 3lb but still not discounted
runners.spotlight: Gained a C&D win in January and very nearly added another three weeks ago; nudged up a further 3lb for that but he has won off his mark before.

runners.owner: S McMillan, F Reay & A D Brown

prev_owners.owner: D D Oakes & A D Brown

runners.comment: Respectable efforts recently without suggesting he's a winner in waiting
runners.spotlight: Notched three wins at the beginning of 2025 but hasn't hit the same heights this year, for all he's reached the frame a few times between 1m and 1m4f; this is competitive and his wait for another win will probably go on.

quotes.race: Hull FC Rugby League Takeover Day Handicap
quotes.quote: The pace of the race didn't suit him last time. Urban Road is improving, the penny has only just dropped with him - Alan Brown, trainer.

runners.comment: 1m2f course win last autumn but found out off higher marks since; off four months
runners.spotlight: 1m2f course winner in September but higher marks found him out in two subsequent visits last year; others are preferred back from four months off.

stable_tour.quote: A fun horse who won in the ­Sunday Series at the start of the season. We aimed him at the ­series bonuses, but it's tough. He regained the winning thread at Newcastle on Monday and may now go for a handicap at Ayr's Western meeting. 10-09-25

racecards.verdict: The way in which SAYTARR (nap) travelled last time suggests he can cope with another rise in the weights and make it 3-3 for this yard.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Saytarr, 5/1 Brewing, 13/2 Sir Paul Ramsey, 8/1 Nyman, 9/1 Flying Fletcher, 10/1 Rogue Encore,  Mr Mistoffelees, 16/1 Harry The Rogue, 20/1 Maestro Bernstein,  Urban Road,  Izzari, 25/1 Degale

racecards.race_name: SBK: Dont Settle For Less Handicap

runners.owner: T S Ingham & Mrs Liz Ingham
runners.comment: Front-runner who is a C&D winner; ended 2025 with a good third at Southwell; off 148 days
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who is a C&D winner and added another AW success at Southwell (7f) last July; ended 2025 with a good third back at Southwell (7f again) in October; formerly trained by Ann Duffield; claims if ready to roll after five months off.

runners.comment: Reappearing C&D winner who has won first time out before; claims
runners.spotlight: C&D winner; reached the frame three times in AW handicaps over this trip at end of last summer and met trouble when sixth over 1m on final start; off for 149 days but he's won off a longer break before.

runners.comment: Now 10 but completed a hat-trick this winter and had an excuse last time (started slowly)
runners.spotlight: No signs of age dimming his enthusiasm, completing a December/January hat-trick (second leg over 1m here); a slow start didn't help when sixth of 12 at Southwell last time and he can be treated as if still in form.

quotes.race: Yorkshire Equine Practice Handicap
quotes.quote: That was a great ride.The instructions were to drop Eligible in and fill him with confidence, he loves passing horses - David Easterby, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Bit disappointing last time, taking his record to 1-16
runners.spotlight: Just one win to his name after 16 starts; made quite an encouraging return from a short break when fourth at Lingfield in January but disappointed back there since (both 7f).

runners.comment: Two 7f turf wins last autumn but unplaced all four AW starts; others preferred on return
runners.spotlight: Ended a long losing run with back-to-back wins from the front over 7f at Catterick last October; found out in a higher grade at Musselburgh on final start; fifth is the best he's managed in four AW starts (all here) and it's likely best to look elsewhere on reappearance.

quotes.race: Jill Willows Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought Mudamer would have won before now - he's very talented. I think the cheekpieces have helped him a lot because he hit the front at York and then just shut down. It's just made him focus. He's made hard work of it on what he does at home. I have a horse, Scottish Summit, rated 91 and this fella will kick him into touch without even coming off the bridle - Geoff Harker, trainer.

runners.comment: Third AW win when shading close finish over C&D last month; only sixth since
runners.spotlight: Landed a third win on AW when shading a tight finish over C&D last month but only a respectable sixth at Wolverhampton off this mark since.

quotes.race: Roflow Environmental Engineering Specialist Ventilation Services Handicap
quotes.quote: It's been a long time between drinks for Benacre but he's a bit of a favourite at home and I'm delighted to see him get his head back in front. He had a frustrating campaign last year and, in hindsight when we were trying different things, we were going in the wrong direction in terms of trip. After his comeback run at Chelmsford this year we thought coming back to seven [furlongs] was worth a try - Charlie Johnston, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Two 6f wins last month; second to subsequent three-time winner over 7f since; good shout
runners.spotlight: Hold-up performer who was successful over 6f at Wolverhampton and Southwell last month; proved himself at 7f when his strong finish only just failed to reel in the thriving Goldmoyne (won three times since) back at Southwell last time; it's likely he's still on a good mark.

runners.comment: Four 6f turf wins in excellent first year with Harriet Bethell; also second over 7f on AW
runners.spotlight: Landed a fourth success of a productive first season with Harriet Bethell when comfortably seeing off 12 rivals at Pontefract in October; all those wins came at 6f but he was also second over 7f at Chelmsford last summer; no surprise were he to improve again this year.

quotes.race: pricedup.bet Handicap
quotes.quote: I was happy to get a nice lead and there was a good pace to aim at. City Captain has got a bit of knee action and really appreciated the bit of dig in the ground. He won cosy and I think he could improve in time  - Danny Tudhope, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's won three times this season and is very exciting. It's not his downfall, but he needs soft ground as he's quite a big three-year-old and not a particularly good mover. I don't want to run him on anything quicker than soft or good or soft. He came back and was a bit sore after the interference he got at Doncaster last week and won't go for the Ayr Gold Cup now, but he'll be out again before the end of the season. He'll be even better next year when he's grown into himself. 17-09-25

runners.comment: All four wins over 6f here, including latest start, but he does have placed form at 7f
runners.spotlight: All four wins over 6f here, gaining the latest when leading late on 15 days ago; placed a few times at 7f and ought to remain very competitive off only 2lb higher.

runners.comment: His win three weeks ago took his C&D record to 4-5; looks sure to go well again
runners.spotlight: Has an excellent 4-5 record over C&D, with three of the wins coming since early February; had a bit to spare last time so a 4lb rise shouldn't prevent another bold bid.

runners.comment: Promising reappearance third over 6f here 15 days and the return to 7f should suit
runners.spotlight: Spring has been quite a productive time for him which provides hope that he can build on a promising reappearance third over 6f here 15 days ago; has raced mainly at 7f/1m in recent years so the step back up in trip should help if anything.

quotes.race: Watch Racing TV In Stunning HD Handicap
quotes.quote: Havana Prince is a grand little horse. He may not be the classiest, but he makes up for that by being tough and genuine. That was as quick ground as he wants and you won't be seeing him again until there's a bit of rain. He loves Redcar and Ripon, so we'll wait for the rain and won't have to go out of Yorkshire to find more winning opportunities - Tony Coyle, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Amy Washbourne Bloom Digitally Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: I would have been unlucky as I got hampered out of the gate and Havana Prince had to work hard to get into a good position. I thought we got racing plenty early and I needed the line in the last fifty yards - David Nolan, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

prev_owners.owner: Ursa Major Racing Ltd And G Tuer

runners.comment: 6f Leicester win last October but last to Mudamer at Catterick 11 days later and off since
runners.spotlight: Well backed when winning over 6f at Leicester (good to soft) last October but last of ten to Mudamer at Catterick 11 days later and off since; others are preferred.

quotes.race: Ripon Yorkshire's Garden Racecourse Handicap
quotes.quote: Wreck It Ryley has done it well. I was just waiting for the gap to appear. He's run in blinkers a few times before and they do help him because he's a bit behind the bridle normally. He keeps breaking half a stride too slowly, but he's soon there on the heels of the leaders and he was there when I needed him. I had plenty of horse underneath me to commit and go - Dale Swift, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He has been a busy lad this season with 14 runs and two wins. On his latest start at Ayr they virtually trotted to the three-furlong marker before sprinting. He wasn't best positioned for that but he came home well to win and has gone up only 2lb for it, which I thought was fair. I'm hopeful he can add to his successes again this season [ran at Musselburgh on Tuesday night after the Weekender went to press]. 30-08-23

racecards.verdict: Thriving pair CARGIN BHUI and Flowstate might fight this out, with the former narrowly preferred.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Cargin Bhui, 11/2 Flowstate, 6/1 City Captain, 13/2 Beale Street, 8/1 Philanthropist,  Best Rate, 9/1 Benacre, 12/1 Master Richard, 14/1 Eligible, 16/1 Havana Prince, 33/1 Mudamer,  Wreck It Ryley

racecards.race_name: SBK Betting Podcast Handicap

runners.comment: Off for 566 days but displayed significant promise on AW as a 2yo; betting informative
runners.spotlight: Made a winning start to his AW career in a 5f Chelmsford nursery in August 2024 and shaped well when pitched into a Group 3 over 6f at Kempton just a week later, impressing with his headway into contention before his effort flattened out (raced keenly); not seen since but retains plenty of potential as a sprint handicapper, for all it would be understandable were this outing to be needed; the betting should provide more clues in that regard.

runners.comment: Useful as 2yo but hasn't shown he retains that ability in two comeback runs for new yard
runners.spotlight: Useful as 2yo for Archie Watson but hasn't shown he retains that level of ability in two recent comeback outings for Julie Camacho.

runners.owner: Ms Janelle Cao, Ross Harmon & Partner
runners.comment: Beat Sports Coach to win at Southwell last month but only fourth to same rival there since
runners.spotlight: Had Sports Coach behind in second when back to winning ways at Southwell (5f) last month but only a respectable fourth to that same rival back there since.

quotes.race: Free Bets With BetUK Bet Club Handicap
quotes.quote: Master Of My Fate jumped really well and the more he's racing the more he's improving. I'd like to think when he gets back on turf he will do the same - Jason Hart, jockey.

quotes.race: Trevor Woods Memorial British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands A, B, C & D) Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Master Of My Fate been training well at home. I'm very pleased with how he did it. You can only beat what's put in front of you, but we've always liked him and I was delighted to see him win - John Quinn, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He beat very little when winning at Pontefract on his debut but he beat them very well and also ran well in a novice at Lingfield, even though he wasn't in love with that track. Then it didn't look like he stayed 6f at Newcastle. I'd imagine we'll drop him back to 5f and he could be one for decent sprint handicaps. He's been gelded and I think that will help him. 20-03-24

runners.comment: Good second at Wolverhampton in December but below par at Southwell since; off 82 days
runners.spotlight: Won twice on Tapeta early last year; ran well from 5lb out of the weights when second of six at Wolverhampton (5f) just before Christmas but never involved at Southwell at the beginning of January; freshened up since; same yard runs Sports Coach.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Now EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Blinky is quick, he can cope with that ground and Kieran [Shoemark, jockey] said he'd be better suited being held on for longer. We can freshen him up now and get him ready for Royal Ascot - Ed Walker, trainer.

runners.comment: Solid AW record, finishing second then first over 5f at Southwell this year; big player
runners.spotlight: Built on his Southwell reappearance second to Master Of My Fate when seeing off five rivals (including Master Of My Fate and Reigning Profit) back there 13 days ago; compiling a good AW record and ought to go well again.

stable_tour.quote: I think he's a Group sprinter in the making. He won his last two races on the all-weather very well and will go to Bath for a £45,000 three-year-old handicap on Sunday. If it comes up very soft he'll wait for a 0-90 at Thirsk, then he'll go for the Westow at York. 03-04-24

runners.comment: Promising second on 6f AW debut and reappearance five weeks ago; enters calculations
runners.spotlight: Has largely run well in defeat since scoring twice over 6f on testing turf in autumn 2024, including when second of 12 on Southwell AW debut and reappearance (gelded) five weeks ago; led until approaching the final furlong at the Nottinghamshire venue so should be speedy enough to cope with the return to 5f; enters calculations.

runners.comment: Likely needed last month's first outing for Paul Midgley and should last longer this time
runners.spotlight: All four wins when trained by Craig Lidster; drew a blank for Ivan Furtado last year but was second over 6f at Kempton on final start; faded as if his first outing for this yard was needed when eighth of 11 over 6f here 15 days ago; should last longer this time.

runners.comment: Good third at Southwell last autumn but below that level in two starts there this year
runners.spotlight: Won twice over 5f on turf last year; also a good third over 5f on Southwell's Tapeta in September but below that level in two outings there this year, weakening quickly last time; others are more persuasive.

stable_tour.quote: He was unlucky after winning his novice first time out at York because he never really had his ground. He loves it fast and even good to soft is no good to him. He's an out-and-out 5f horse who is up to winning some nice races. 04-04-24

runners.comment: Two C&D wins belatedly switched to AW at the end of 2025; could still be feasibly treated
runners.spotlight: Had his first 30 starts on turf but reacted well to a belated switch to AW at the end of 2025, winning twice over C&D; the latter success came in quite smooth fashion so he could still be feasibly treated off 6lb higher if fully primed after 104 days off.

quotes.race: Betonline At BetGoodwin Cock O'The North EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Tiriac ran very well at Newmarket the other day, it was a good horse who beat him there. He's a full-brother to Nastase who won the Rockingham Stakes - Mick Channon, trainer

runners.comment: Hampered and better than result behind Sports Coach on return; 3lb below last win mark
runners.spotlight: The winner of three turf handicaps in 2025, the latest off 3lb higher; stopped in his run on a couple of occasions and shaped better than the result when 2l fifth of six to reopposing Sports Coach on 5f Southwell reappearance 13 days ago; might be worth chancing.

quotes.race: Welcome Racing TV Members Handicap
quotes.quote: Reigning Profit was a bit slower away than we'd hoped but it worked out well in the end. He likes it here - Ruth Carr, trainer.

quotes.race: Ripon Races Ladies Day 22nd June Handicap
quotes.quote: He did it well. Reigning Profit broke very quickly so I travelled strongly through the race and I think he was just getting a little tired near the line - James Sullivan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap (Round 3)
quotes.quote: Reigning Profit is usually a good eater and he's a solid sprinter so I see no reason why he shouldn't go to Goodwood on Friday - Ruth Carr, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A solid sprinter who had a busy 2024 running 20 times, scoring at Wolverhampton and Hamilton and finishing runner-up four times. A turning track over 5f suits him best. There's a race for him at Pontefract on April 14. 09-04-25

runners.comment: The sort Ruth Carr will do well with but whether it's first time up remains to be seen
runners.spotlight: Lost his form for Des Donovan last autumn but that means he has a reduced mark to work with on this first outing for Ruth Carr after a 10,000gns sale in October; the sort this yard will gets wins from but whether it's at the first time of asking remains to be seen.

runners.comment: Lightly raced; good second over C&D last year; too keen on 6f return; retains potential
runners.spotlight: Good second in competitive races in her first two handicaps last summer, latterly a Racing League event over C&D; pulled too hard when only sixth of seven on 6f Southwell reappearance but this lightly raced filly retains potential and the return to 5f looks a good move.

racecards.verdict: Sports Coach should go well but REIGNING PROFIT looked a threat to him when hampered late on at Southwell recently and gets the nod.

racecards.race_name: #wearahatday Supporting Brain Tumour Awareness Month Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Turnaround is possible returned to forecast good ground
runners.spotlight: Promise shown in good-ground bumper at Worcester has not been backed up in two maiden hurdles on softer going; turnaround is possible returned to forecast faster conditions.

runners.comment: Never figured on rules debut
runners.spotlight: Fairly exposed maiden pointer in Ireland and never figured at Ayr (2m) on the switch to rules.

runners.comment: Turnaround is more likely to occur in handicaps shortly
runners.spotlight: Regressive RPRs since debut promise (bumper); modest fifth to stablemate at Southwell (2m) most recently; turnaround is more likely to occur in handicaps shortly.

runners.comment: Likely to improve back down in trip with 2m4f reappearance under his belt
runners.spotlight: Twice-raced and nicely bred 7yo who gives the impression he's likely to improve back down in distance with 2m4f reappearance under his belt; interesting in this second hurdles attempt.

runners.comment: Made the frame in bumpers; less solid on hurdles form
runners.spotlight: Made the frame in two bumpers but looks less solid on hurdles form that comprises a late fall (6l down at the time) and poor effort; however, certainly has ability so could go well.

runners.comment: Still needs to prove he can back up debut form (bumper)
runners.spotlight: Both starts at Newcastle, finishing fourth in bumper then pulled up (seemingly not beaten entirely by the 2m4f trip) in novice hurdle; still needs to prove he can back up the debut form.

runners.comment: Poor form in two hurdles attempts
runners.spotlight: Record of 1-5 in Irish points; poor form in two attempts over hurdles.

runners.comment: Galway bumper winner; joined new connections for 82,000GBP; one of the main players
runners.spotlight: Prevailed by just under 1l in Galway bumper (yielding) in sole start for James Conheady; form well advertised by the third since; joined new connections for 82,000GBP; one of the main players.

runners.comment: Has consistent form at 2m; holds solid and leading claims back down in distance
runners.spotlight: Weakened into modest third over 2m3f at Catterick last time; consistent at 2m otherwise in bumpers and over hurdles; holds solid and leading claims back down in distance.

stable_tour.quote: He probably wants two and a half miles, but he was a bit keen when chasing home what is a fair horse in Un Sens A La Vie at Market Rasen in October so we kept him at the minimum trip at Exeter last time. He bumped into another nice horse in Lisbane Park there, but it was another solid run. 18-11-25

runners.breeder: Mrs J A Niven & Mrs Diana Ewart
runners.owner: Clova Farms And P D Niven
runners.comment: Similar type to Finbarr; hood applied
runners.spotlight: Twice-raced 5yo who has a similar profile to Finbarr; chance depends on how well he responds to first-time hood.

runners.comment: Showed some promise with fifth of nine in Kelso bumper; may improve
runners.spotlight: Took a good hold, despite wearing a hood, but managed to show some promise with fifth of nine in Kelso bumper; may improve, especially if settling better in the retained headgear.

runners.breeder: J C Haimet, Mme E Petit, Mme H Pet
runners.comment: Regressive form in bumpers; hood fitted
runners.spotlight: Regressive form in bumpers; failed to beat a rival last time; needs major improvement for the switch to hurdles and fitting of hood.

runners.comment: Record of 2-4 on Flat; has failed to shine in two hurdles attempts
runners.spotlight: Has failed to shine in two attempts over hurdles and may be more interesting in handicaps shortly; otherwise retains potential judged on Flat record (2-4; best RPR 85).

runners.comment: Trailed home last of nine on hurdles debut
runners.spotlight: Finished third in a couple of Flat races for previous yard but lacked fluency and trailed home last of nine at Catterick on the switch to this code; tongue-tie applied.

runners.breeder: Societe Civile De L'Ecurie De Meautry
runners.comment: Failed to finish at Doncaster (British/hurdles debut) but should be capable of better
runners.spotlight: Has a smart Flat pedigree; showed some promise under that code in sole French start; failed to finish in Doncaster maiden hurdle (2m) but should be capable of better; one to keep an eye on.

racecards.race_name: Watch The Grand National On Racing TV Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Only 1lb above last winning hurdles mark and Edward Vaughan takes off bonus 7lb
runners.spotlight: Mixed results (5FP4) since switched to chasing but is now only 1lb above last winning hurdles mark and Edward Vaughan takes off a bonus 7lb; possibilities, provided he stays returned to 3m.

runners.breeder: Sarl Elevage Du Haras De Bourgeauville
runners.owner: Readers & Wiggy, The 8 Amigos & J Burns
runners.comment: Ran well in this race last year but has gained all jumps wins at Market Rasen
runners.spotlight: Veteran who was a close second in this contest last year but is by no means certain to go one better, having gained all six jumps wins at Market Rasen; inconsistent results since last success.

quotes.race: Chris Coley BEM Celebration Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Giovanni Change used to boot hurdles out the ground but that was his best round of jumping, he was superb and he's given his owners such a wonderful time. He was on my list at the sales a few years ago but I was worried he'd be too expensive. I was told he's blind in one eye, asymmetrical behind and is a terrible box-walker, so I thought at least I might be able to afford him. We took his eye out and we couldn't train him and he wouldn't eat, but we've got outdoor stables now and he's perfect in there. That's his sixth win at this track and he's been remarkable - Mark Walford, trainer.

quotes.race: Victor Lucas Memorial Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Giovanni Change is just the most genuine horse you are ever going to see. He has only got one eye, that is his fifth win now, his fourth at Market Rasen. He just won on the Flat at Ponterfract, what more can you ask for- Neil Readman, co-owner, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: MansionBet #morethanthenational Faller Insurance Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Giovanni Change has run some very good races in defeat in novices and a nice break has worked a treat with him. We've always thought he's a really nice horse, he has some good novice hurdle form that stacks up and hopefully we can pick up a nice race with him - Mark Walford, trainer.

quotes.race: Europe Hotel Killarney INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: We have actually had Giovanni Change a while but he's been a bit of a slow burner. He definitely wouldn't like it any quicker. I'm surprised by that and he will be a nice horse going forward for the future. The further he goes the better I'd say, and he might even make into a winter horse. I wouldn't be afraid of slower ground as he has a fair knee action - trainer Emmet Mullins.

runners.owner: K P Marsh Plastering & Interiors Ltd
runners.comment: Pulled up in both starts since opening his chase account in Hereford contest
runners.spotlight: Pulled up in both starts since opening his chase account in Hereford contest; still seeking first success above Class 5; cheekpieces added.

runners.comment: May benefit from this switch to chasing; attractively treated on Irish point form
runners.spotlight: Still a maiden but may benefit from this switch to chasing, combined with first-time headgear, and looks attractively handicapped off current mark judged on some of his Irish point form; interesting.

runners.comment: Heavy ground provides an excuse for latest effort; still unexposed in handicaps
runners.spotlight: Point and hunter chase winner who is still unexposed in handicaps; heavy ground provides an excuse for latest effort; scored at Sedgefield (3m2f) the time before and remains of interest.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Margaret Coppola & Mrs Dianne Sayer

runners.comment: On a handy mark but has been absent for 13 months; market helpful
runners.spotlight: Scored off slightly higher marks twice, including over C&D, in November 2024 when under the care of Dianne Sayer; returns from 13-month absence; market may prove best guide.

quotes.race: Racing TV Profits Returned To Racing Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase (Go North Red Rum Qual')
quotes.quote: Cardamon Hill is a good-ground horse and we might as well keep him going. There's a 0-125 over three miles for him on November 28 at Musselburgh, which is his owners' local track - Dianne Sayer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well in a few points for Colin McKeever and will run in a bumper sooner rather than later. 18-10-22

runners.comment: Combination of switch to fences and first-time headgear may have a positive effect
runners.spotlight: Eight-race maiden whose hurdles form has dipped since a consistent spell; however, this combination of a switch to fences and first-time headgear may have a positive effect; bred to make a chaser.

runners.comment: May build on latest effort as he remains unexposed at this distance; in the mix
runners.spotlight: Point/hurdles winner who hasn't strictly improved in two chase attempts but may build on latest effort (3m) as he remains unexposed at this distance; visor replaces the cheekpieces worn of late; in the mix.

quotes.race: Join The 20 Club At Huntingdon Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Youdecide has enjoyed the step up in trip here and will make a nice horse next year when he strengthens up - Tom David, trainer's assistant.

runners.comment: Five chase wins, the most recent off current mark in this race last year; solid claims
runners.spotlight: Takes on possible improvers in this field; otherwise a solid candidate who has five chase wins on his CV, the most recent off current mark in this race 12 months ago; last two efforts show he's back in form; respected.

quotes.race: Racing TV Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: It was lovely to get back on Mixedwave. I'm very fortunate that the owners are supportive and Pam (Sly) is so loyal and a lovely lady. He's massive and not a hurdler, so when he came to chasing he soon found his form and keeps winning. He's put the race to bed nicely and has managed to stay ahead of the handicapper - Alex Edwards, rider.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Mixedwave deserved that really as he was disqualified the other day although we have moved on from that. He seems to be improving with his racing and hopefully there is more to come -  Pam Sly, trainer.

racecards.verdict: The Verdict comprises THE CLONMEL KID and The Great Escape who are still maidens but may well improve for this switch to chasing.

racecards.race_name: Albert Bartlett Triple Crown Series Handicap Hurdle Qualifier)

runners.comment: Has spent most of his career in better handicaps; possibilities dropped sharply in grade
runners.spotlight: Has spent most of his career in better handicaps; on a long losing spell and 0-8 for current yard but shaped encouragingly on penultimate start; possibilities off current mark dropped sharply in grade.

stable_tour.quote: He's run well in many big handicap hurdles, finishing second in a Martin Pipe and third in a Greatwood. He was pulled up in his only chase last season, but he does look like a chaser and we might have another look at that. Otherwise he'll be back into those big handicap hurdles and hopefully it's just a matter of time before he can hit the target in one of them. 22-10-24

runners.comment: Low-mileage 5yo who has a broadly solid record; likely to perform well
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo whose broadly solid record includes point/hurdle wins; placed at Haydock (3m) on handicap debut most recently, while shaping as if this return to shorter will suit; likely to perform well.

prev_owners.owner: Poetry In Motion Syndicate/Gavin Cromwell Racing Limited

runners.comment: Not disgraced last time (second start for new yard) but this is a much deeper race
runners.spotlight: Successful on Flat in Denmark and over hurdles in Ireland; not disgraced behind the market leader in 2m4f novice event at Sedgefield (second start for new yard) most recently; this is a much deeper race.

stable_tour.quote: He originates from Denmark, which is very unusual - you won't find many of them around. He was with Gavin Cromwell and is one that we're looking forward to. We'll try to find a weak maiden or novice hurdle and he'll also run back on the Flat once we get an official rating. He's shown plenty of speed. 04-03-26

runners.comment: Sole attempt in cheekpeices resulted in creditable second at Kempton on penultimate start
runners.spotlight: Soft ground provides an excuse for two defeats of late; sole attempt in cheekpieces resulted in good second at Kempton (2m5f) on penultimate start; could go well in the reapplied headgear.

runners.breeder: Earl De Cordelles & Earl La Dariole
runners.comment: Solid performances (132) since having wind surgery and wearing cheekpieces; big player
runners.spotlight: Maiden prior to showing improvement with solid performances (132) since having wind surgery and wearing cheekpieces, most recently beaten only narrowly at Ascot (2m7f) three months ago; that form has been franked by the winner since; goes well fresh and holds strong claims returned to the scene of his October win.

runners.comment: Form stacks up well; open to progress now handicapping; could be on a very workable mark
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage maiden whose form (point/bumper/hurdles) stacks up well; debut in this sphere was behind a horse who has since run well in the Turners; open to progress now handicapping over a new trip with tongue-tie fitted; interesting contender who could be on a very workable opening mark.

runners.comment: May have a race in him but doesn't appear to be crying out for this step back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Represents the Constitution Hill connections; record is 0-5 but his two placed efforts, both over 2m, suggest there may be a race of this nature in him; however, doesn't appear to be crying out for this step back up in distance on handicap debut.

stable_tour.quote: He ran in a point-to-point in Ireland, finishing sixth, and he's a big, classy Blue Bresil gelding. He was very free, but I don't think that's his norm and therefore we're ignoring that. He jumps very well and he'll go straight over hurdles. I like him. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Knuckled down well in C&D handicap on Boxing Day and is open to further improvement
runners.spotlight: Lacked fluency but knuckled down well to prevail by a neck in C&D handicap on Boxing Day when last seen, adding to his Irish point win and taking overall record to 2-4; open to further improvement, especially if jumping better; respected.

runners.comment: By no means certain to follow up a fortuitous win at Fakenham; this is a stronger race
runners.spotlight: May still have more to offer for Dan Skelton but is by no means certain to follow up a fortuitous win at Fakenham (2m4f) where she was gifted the race when the clear leader exited; now 1lb higher in a stronger event.

stable_tour.quote: She has some nice form to her name and looks like a staying hurdler for this season, hopefully competing with the better mares. We'll get her started in a handicap and hopefully she'll progress nicely. 10-11-25

She's a quality filly off the Flat and has never been out of the first two for us. She was a little bit sketchy with her jumping on her last run at Doncaster. The quicker pace on better ground just caught her out in that regard and she wasn't as fluent as I'd have liked. However, once the pace had settled turning in, she made up ground very nicely to finish second. I'm not sure where she'll go next but it might be Cheltenham for the April meeting. 19-03-25

runners.comment: Gained his Plumpton success in small field; only midfield in deeper contest since
runners.spotlight: Gained his Plumpton success (2m4f) in small field and was only midfield in a deeper race at Wincanton later in February; opposed in another competitive contest.

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras D'Enki
runners.comment: 2-3 for new stable, the wins in December; upped in grade but may well improve further
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish 7yo who is 2-3 for new stable, the wins in Class 5 handicaps at Lingfield (2m3f) and Leicester (2m4f) in December; now 7lb higher and upped in grade but may well improve further; helps to give Ben Pauling a robust hand.

runners.owner: Mrs P Bond, Magniers, Mrs P Shanahan
runners.comment: Form dipped last time (handicap debut) but he's in good hands and may do better still
runners.spotlight: Four-race maiden whose form dipped in Ayr handicap (2m4f) most recently; however, he's in good hands and may do better still; remains attractively treated on his first couple of efforts.

stable_tour.quote: He went a bit weak on us after running with promise at Chepstow, but there's been no major issues. He's a big horse who has taken time to fill his frame, but he's done well over the summer and is one we're looking forward to seeing over hurdles. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Last-time win took her Wetherby record to 3121; brings solid claims to this stronger race
runners.spotlight: Justified favouritism in 2m3f mares' handicap most recently, taking Wetherby record to 3121; faces a stiffer assignment in this field, back against males, but holds solid claims kept to this venue.

quotes.race: Watch William Hill Inside Track Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We'd been a little bit disappointed with Just Call Me Lucy's hurdle runs as her bumper form was strong but this was a big step up and the longer distance helped her, she jumped a lot better. She just idled in front - Mark Walford, trainer.

runners.comment: Took well to first-time hood in Ludlow maiden over 2m; may build on that success
runners.spotlight: Benefited from first-time hood at Ludlow (2m) in latest attempt in maiden hurdles; may build on that success and show further progress in the retained headgear, provided he's as effective back up in trip.

runners.comment: Registered an easy success at Doncaster on handicap debut when last seen; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Registered an easy success in Class 5 contest at Doncaster (2m3f) on handicap debut when last seen four months ago, opening his hurdles account; now 12lb higher and upped in grade but may be capable of further progress in this sphere; not ruled out.

runners.owner: M Blades, Craggs, Clark And Cambridge
runners.comment: Faces a difficult task and has never won away from Hexham
runners.spotlight: Below par at Ayr last time, ending a consistent spell of form; rebound looks possible but this is a difficult task and he's still seeking a first win away from Hexham.

quotes.race: Kirkstyle Inn & Sportsmans Rest Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I was really pleased with Forest Blaze as we've always thought he'd be a nice horse. We were very happy with his run over two miles last time as we expected the step up in trip to really suit. He's got a couple of entries in the next few days, but I'm not sure if he'll take them up as he's got the job done now - Mark Walford, trainer.

runners.comment: Holds very weak claims on his form since switched to handicap hurdles
runners.spotlight: Gained sole success in Sedgefield maiden; holds weak claims on his form since switched to handicap hurdles; yard appears to have a better chance with Mandarb.

runners.comment: Irish 5yo whose chance largely depends on how well he responds to headgear
runners.spotlight: Irish maiden who looks far from solid on form; receives plenty of weight all round but chance largely depends on how well he responds to first-time headgear.

racecards.verdict: The percentage call goes to BRAS D'OR, ahead of Daylatedollarshort in a competitive and very interesting handicap.
